item.title: RM-VLM: From Natural-Language Task Descriptions to Vision-Grounded Reward Machines
item.description: Reward machines (RMs) have been proposed as a reward formulation in reinforcement learning (RL) to capture non-Markovian tasks where credit assignment depends on history. By representing reward functions as automata, RMs expose the task's temporal structure and allow such rewards to be handled within a Markovian framework. However, they assume a labelling function, a proposition-grounding oracle for observations, which must be manually engineered for each environment, limiting their wider applicability. item.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
item.description: Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from. In-context learning (ICL) avoids this coupling but has not matched trained policies, because a demonstration recorded in another scene carries no feedback from the world the robot currently faces. We observe that what an agent learns in context is semantic, recording task steps and object roles rather than visual appearance, so experience gathered in one world transfers to another. Based on this insight, we propose World In-Context Learning (WICL), a paradigm in — 来源：github · verge_ai · arxiv — 原文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12885v1

item.title: Introducing Usul - an easier way to express your NN using maths? [P]
item.description: SO, Usul-cpp is a library I've written in C++, it is based around allowing data scientists to create their models without heavy libraries such as tensorflow, and just express their models using maths, and Usul will handle the rest. There is builtin tensor support, auto-grad, back-prop and its quite fast. I wrote it because, it seemed less mystifying to read maths instead of a random class that supposedly does something. item.title: Agentic Attribution of Cloud Resource Ownership
item.description: Security tools raise findings across cloud environments, and AI agents now investigate and prioritize them. A finding is still resolved by people: it has to reach the people responsible for fixing it and accountable for the resource it concerns. Ownership is the organizational context that decides who that is. Where recorded, it is declared by hand in configuration management databases or owner tags and goes stale unless kept current; accounts are shared, and automation creates much of the infrastructure. item.title: Automated Knowledge Acquisition Pipeline for Disassembly Instructions: A Comparison of NLP and Generative AI Frameworks
item.description: The push towards circularity and Re-X principles presents a challenge to SMEs, particularly due to increasing product complexity that impedes the adoption of disassembly automation. Our goal is to transform natural language text into a structured, curated and machine-readable format. item.title: OPSRL-SSP: Optimistic Posterior Sampling for Stochastic Shortest Path with Minimax-Optimal Regret
item.description: We study online reinforcement learning for the stochastic shortest path (SSP) problem with unknown transition dynamics. Although existing posterior-sampling methods perform well empirically on SSPs, their regret guarantees do not achieve the minimax-optimal order. We address this limitation by proposing OPSRL-SSP, an optimistic posterior-sampling algorithm for the SSP setting. The algorithm operates in epochs and uses a logarithmic, time-dependent schedule for the number of posterior samples.
